names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 18 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Στέφανος Πατριάρχης Κωνσταντινούπολης», with the rank word and the see left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 17. мај ст. ст., „Свети Стефан, патријарх цариградски.“ Свети is not a rank; „патријарх цариградски“ is the rank and the see, which this corpus puts in `types` as `patriarch` and in `office` as Patriarch of Constantinople, and **stripping a rank and a see to reach the stored form is the reading BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §6 asks be said in the note** — here it leaves a bare forename with nothing beside it, the father, the brother, Photius and the years all being in the body. **So this is a deliberate twelfth joining of the largest fold this corpus has in Cyrillic**: `foldchk.py` returned eleven folders holding „Стефан“ before a line was drafted, and the plain gate run already prints them as one `?` row. There is no fuller form on the page to prefer, and a form a reader builds is what §6 forbids. The fold is read in this batch's commit message.

The nominative the day page's own `/name/` link carries in its `title`, «Святитель Стефан Константинопольский, патриарх», with «Святитель» and the trailing «патриарх» left off — the latter is the `patriarch` this folder carries in `types`, with the see in `office`. The day's own line declines him «Свт. Стефана , Патриарха Константинопольского (893).» `fk.mjs` on «Стефан Константинопольский» returned NONE before the write; the corpus's read fold «стефан», of thirteen holders, already counts this folder among them through a shorter form, and storing a longer string adds no member to it.

birth.note: saint.gr: «γεννήθηκε το 867 μ.Χ.», and its head line reads «Αγιος Στεφανος Πατριαρχης Κωνσταντινουπολης (867 - 893)».

death.note: saint.gr: «Πέθανε το Μάιο του 893 μ.Χ. σε ηλικία 26 ετών και ενταφιάσθηκε στη μονή του Αγίου Γεωργίου «εν τω Δευτέρω»».

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 17 мая ст. ст. — «Свт. Стефана , Патриарха Константинопольского (893).»

attestations.note: The same menologion day the folder already keeps for the Greek, and the same man: the younger son of the emperor Basil the Macedonian, brother of Leo the Wise, raised to the see of Constantinople in 886 when Photius had to leave it, dead in 893. `dates` were not touched — the folder carries a birth of 867 and a death of 893 off saint.gr, and this page gives the same death year and no birth. The Russian adds the burial place, the Sikellion monastery, and says he was watchful over his flock, merciful, a defender of the defenceless, a carer for widows and orphans and marked by extreme abstinence. His life page gives one day only, «17 мая». The day page prints no hymn for him. azbyka.ru was not read.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 18ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Στέφανος Πατριάρχης Κωνσταντινούπολης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 18 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **He is none of the corpus's Stephens**: a son of the emperor Basil the Macedonian and of Eudokia, born 867, pupil and synkellos of Photius the Great, patriarch from 886 under his brother Leo the Wise, dead in May 893 at twenty-six. **The display name drops the see**, which `office` carries, and keeps nothing else, the page giving him no epithet. **Photius has a folder and is linked.** **His parents, his brother Leo VI, and the monastery of Saint George «εν τω Δευτέρω», called the Sykiotes house, have none** and are named without links. **No `locations` object.** **The page's own supposition is recorded as one**: «Πιθανόν θεωρείται, ότι επί της πατριαρχείας του εκδόθηκε το πρώτο Σύνταγμα των επισκόπων του Οικουμενικού Θρόνου» — it is thought probable that the first register of the bishops of the Ecumenical Throne was issued in his patriarchate. No hymn is printed.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 30.05.2026 (17. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети Стефан, патријарх цариградски.“

attestations.note: **The day list could not see this folder**, because the Greek row keeps him on the menologion **18/5** and the Prologue keeps him on the **17/5**, and the list matches on the menologion number; it offered fifteen folders and not this one. He was found by `ls saints | grep -iE 'stephen|stefan'` and by reading the two Constantinopolitan Stephens, which is the third day running that command has caught what the list could not. **The identification is exact and leaves nothing open**: „Син цара Василија Македонца и брат цара Лава Мудрог. На престо патријаршијски дошао је после Фотија“ against a folder whose life has him the son of Basil the Macedonian and of Eudokia, pupil and synkellos of Photius, patriarch under his brother Leo the Wise — and whose `related` already holds `basil-the-macedonian` and `photius-of-constantinople`. **He is not `stephen-ii-of-constantinople`**, who is kept on 18 July, came from Amaseia, and died in 928. **Two days and two churches, and it is not a conflict**: the Greek row stays on 18 May and was not moved. **A DISAGREEMENT OF THREE YEARS THAT HAS NO FIELD.** „управљао Црквом Божјом од 889-893. године“ gives **889** for the start of the patriarchate, where saint.gr says „he took the patriarchal throne, in the year 886“. **It is neither a birth nor a death, so there is no `dates` field for it** — the schema has `birth`, `death` and `floruit` and nothing for an office held — and `dates` is therefore **untouched**: `birth` 867 and `death` „May 893“ both stand, and **the two books agree on the 893**. Both years for the accession are in the added paragraph and neither is chosen. **New besides**: only that he **reposed in peace and stood before the Lord whom he greatly loved**, where saint.gr says he died at twenty-six and was buried in the monastery of Saint George; this is a three-sentence entry and the honest account of it is that it corroborates and adds one year that cannot be stored. `types` untouched — Свети is no rank and „патријарх цариградски“ is the `patriarch` in `types` and the `office` the folder already holds. **His father and his brother take no rows of their own from this entry**: `basil-the-macedonian` is a `related` row already, and the emperor Leo the Wise has no folder, as the 16 May entry for `nicholas-the-mystikos` also found. No `locations`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
